key_insight: A polynomial-time classical algorithm can efficiently simulate single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, even at scales previously treated as hardware-challenging.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the classical barrier for evaluating chemistry-inspired quantum circuits and helps benchmark whether quantum devices are truly outperforming optimized classical methods.
method: Derive a polynomial-time classical procedure for computing the circuit energy for any single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow ansatz.
Remove dependence on hardware locality constraints, enabling simulation of large circuits directly on a classical laptop.
Use fast simulation to optimize the circuit and search for lower-energy configurations than the reported experiment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproducing the largest 77-qubit, 10,570-gate experiment in under a minute on a laptop and achieving a lower ground-state energy than the experiment.
watch_item: The result applies to single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, so extension to deeper or more general ansätze may require new ideas.
paper_title: Efficient classical simulation of large-scale unitary cluster Jastrow circuits
